title: Long Short-Term Memory
before: Recurrent nets existed but gradients vanished over long sequences, so they forgot.
problem: Errors propagated backwards through many steps shrink to nothing, capping memory at a few words.
breakthrough: A gated memory cell that can hold a value unchanged across many steps until a gate decides to alter it.
why: It made recurrent networks actually usable, and powered sequence learning until attention displaced it.
next: Seq2seq, neural translation, and ELMo were all built from LSTMs.
inherits: Gating as a way to control what information persists, and the long-range dependency problem attention later solved differently.
